_: Authored prose. The composer selects which of this appears and for whom; it never writes any of it. This is what makes the safety property structural rather than procedural — the model cannot state a falsehood about a dish because it never states anything about a dish.

weighted-sear.label: Weighted sear
weighted-sear.note: Weight is not about speed. It is about contact — holding the whole surface against the pan at once so it browns in one event instead of in patches.
weighted-sear.whyBody: Browning is a surface event. Every dish here solves the same problem — how to keep food pressed against hot metal long enough for the surface to change — and each one solves it with a different tool. Once you see it as one problem, they stop being separate things to remember.

primer.title:
Press once,
then leave it
primer.body: Anything that lifts food off the pan — moisture, crowding, fidgeting — costs you colour. The weight solves two of those three, and you have to solve the third yourself.
steps: Dry the surface. Wet food steams before it browns.
Give each piece a hand's width of pan.
Press once, then leave it alone for four minutes.
Move it only when it releases on its own.

troubleshooting.cause: Moisture left on the surface, or the pan never got back to temperature after the food went in.
troubleshooting.fix: Lift it out, dry the pan, and go again for four minutes with the weight on.

troubleshooting.cause: The weight is bridging. It is sitting on the high points and never touching the low ones.
troubleshooting.fix: Something flat and heavy, not something heavy. A second pan beats a tin any day.

troubleshooting.symptom: It sticks and tears when you lift it
troubleshooting.cause: You moved it before it was ready. Protein releases on its own when the crust forms.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait. If it resists, it is not done — that is the only test there is.

browning.label: Browning
browning.note: Sugar and protein rearranging under heat. It needs a dry surface and real contact, and it is the difference between cooked and worth eating.
browning.whyBody: Browning is a surface event. Every dish here solves the same problem — how to keep food pressed against hot metal long enough for the surface to change — and each one solves it with a different tool.

primer.title:
Dry surface,
real contact
primer.body: Two conditions, and both are about what is between the food and the pan. Water is the enemy of one and air is the enemy of the other.
steps: Pat it dry, then let it sit uncovered if you have time.
Heat the pan before the fat, and the fat before the food.
Crowd nothing. Steam from one piece lands on its neighbour.

troubleshooting.symptom: The pan smokes within a minute
troubleshooting.cause: Too much oil, or the oil went in before the pan was up to heat.
troubleshooting.fix: A film, not a pool. Most things bring their own fat within two minutes.

troubleshooting.cause: The pan is crowded and the food is steaming in its own moisture.
troubleshooting.fix: Two batches. It is faster than one bad batch you have to fix.

braise.label: Braise
braise.note: Low heat, enough liquid, and long enough that the collagen gives up. Nothing about it rewards attention after the first twenty minutes.
braise.whyBody: The work is at the start and the end. Everything between is the pot doing something you cannot speed up and should not try to.

primer.title:
Start it,
then leave
primer.body: The temptation is to check. Every check costs heat and none of them change the outcome.
steps: Brown first, properly, or the liquid tastes of nothing.
Liquid to two thirds, never covered entirely.
Lid ajar, lowest heat that keeps a lazy bubble.

troubleshooting.cause: It was boiling, not simmering. High heat tightens what low heat relaxes.
troubleshooting.fix: Drop the heat and give it another hour. It will come back.

threadNarrative._: One line per attempt, authored. What the cook changed that time. The composer picks which attempts form a thread; it does not write these.
threadNarrative.041:first: The first one. Pan too crowded, skin steamed.
threadNarrative.041:second: Dry-brined 24 hr instead of 4. Skin finally shattered.
threadNarrative.041:third: Same as last time, but the pan went in the oven to preheat. Best yet.
threadNarrative.032: First time off protein. Same principle, quarter the time.
threadNarrative.033: Started skin-down cold. Rendered further before colour set.
threadNarrative.034: Cast iron on top, no foil. Weight went up to 4 kg.

evidence._: One line per recipe when it appears as evidence under a principle: the tool that dish uses to solve the shared problem.
